section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing another vehicle?
options: a:You may pass another vehicle on a hill or in a curve.,b:You may pass another vehicle by using the shoulder of the highway.,c:You may pass only where it is legal and safe to do so.
note: Never pass on a hill or curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic; do not use the shoulder. Pass only where it is legal and safe.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Proceed if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.,b:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.
note: On a steady green, you may go if the way is clear, but must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection; be prepared to stop if the light changes.

question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability in a way similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that alcohol has.,c:The effect that anger has.,d:None of the above.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in a manner comparable to alcohol. For example, being awake 18 hours can impair driving similar to a BAC of about 0.05%, and 24 hours awake is similar to about 0.10%.

question: Using both lap and shoulder belts together increases survival in a crash. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Properly worn lap and shoulder belts together provide the most protection and reduce the risk of serious injury or death in crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:If there is no oncoming traffic.,b:Yes.,c:No.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean neither lane may cross to pass; you may cross only to turn into a driveway or side road where permitted.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce injury risk in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Limit your driving to weekdays.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash.

question: What characterizes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Looks out for actions of other drivers and anticipates problems.,b:Drives slowly at all times.,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: A good defensive driver stays alert to others' behaviors, anticipates hazards, and adapts speed and position to remain safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is the posted maximum speed limit always the fastest you can legally drive under any conditions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: The posted maximum speed is for ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions (weather, visibility, traffic) require it.

question: Taking drugs together with alcohol typically:
options: a:Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.,b:Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.,c:Increases the risk of causing a crash.
note: Combining drugs and alcohol can multiply impairment and increase the likelihood of a crash.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal narcotics.,b:Only prescription drugs.,c:Both over-the-counter and prescription drugs, as well as illegal drugs.,d:Only allergy medicines.
note: Many legal and illegal drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair driving and make it unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can:
options: a:Return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.,c:Clearly see the road ahead so you can complete the pass safely.
note: You should only pass when you can clearly see the road ahead, can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can safely complete the pass.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline type?
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:Single broken yellow,c:Combination solid and broken yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing by traffic from either direction.

question: Who is required to use seat belts in Minnesota?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:All vehicle occupants as required by law.,c:Only child passengers.,d:Only passengers in the front seat.
note: Minnesota law requires seat belt use; vehicles must be equipped with seat belts and occupants must use them as required.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching on a divided multilane highway, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the signal if other lanes are free.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Slow, provide a clear path by moving if safe, and stop if necessary.,d:Speed up to clear the lane.
note: If you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow and move safely to allow a clear path and stop if necessary so the emergency vehicle can pass.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked on the side of the road, what should you assume?
options: a:The driver may open their door, so use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes as you approach.
note: Assume doors may open; pass slowly and give space when passing parked vehicles to avoid striking someone exiting.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure?
options: a:The passing lane is clear and it is safe to change lanes.,b:You may only pass on the right.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, confirm the lane you will use is clear and signal before changing lanes.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase their speed to clear the intersection.,b:Come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Turn on hazard lights and proceed.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard—slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive and lead to a DUII arrest?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor,b:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or prescription medicines,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint,d:All of the above.
note: Many substances — alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medications — can impair driving ability and can result in arrest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase your speed before turning.,d:Sound your horn instead of signaling.
note: Always signal three to four seconds before turning to communicate your intentions to other road users.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,b:You are moving faster than the bicycle.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
note: Cyclists may need to swerve or avoid hazards; also oncoming traffic may not realize you are passing, so pass with extra caution and give plenty of space.

question: Which actions help lower the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Use tires with proper air pressure.,b:Replace tires that have bad tread.,c:Do not speed when the roads are wet.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk: avoid excessive speed on wet roads, maintain proper tire pressure, and replace tires with worn tread.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle displaying flashing red or blue lights approaches?
options: a:Pull over to the side and come to a complete stop.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.,d:Speed up and get out of the way.
note: Yield the right-of-way: where possible, pull to the right edge of the road and stop; if in an intersection, clear it first then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True — briefly exceeding the speed limit is allowed.,b:False — you must not exceed the posted limit even when passing.,c:Only if the passing lane is clear.,d:Only on a two-lane road.
note: It is illegal to exceed the posted speed limit under any circumstances, including when passing another vehicle.

question: How should you respond when other drivers around you are behaving angrily?
options: a:Avoid eye contact and distance yourself from the situation.,b:React with hand gestures to show disapproval.,c:Accelerate to get away quickly.,d:Confront the driver if they make a mistake.
note: When others are angry you should distance yourself physically and mentally, avoid eye contact, and take actions to reduce risk.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Pull over to the right and stop.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When you hear a siren coming from behind, reduce speed and safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop to clear the way.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using sirens or flashing lights and approaches, the driver must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and slow down.,b:Pull to the right and stop.,c:Pull to the right and turn on their four-way flashers.
note: You must immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop when two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:Either driver may proceed without stopping.
note: When two drivers arrive together at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right and then proceed when safe.

question: Is it lawful to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Driving at night on parking lights alone is unlawful; use your headlights when visibility is reduced.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down because stopping distances are longer and skids more likely.,b:Increase your speed to avoid dust.,c:Come to a complete stop at all times.
note: On unpaved roads reduce speed and drive cautiously because traction is reduced and stopping distances are greater.

question: What's a good general rule for passing slower traffic?
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic so you can see better.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Passing increases collision risk; drive with the flow of traffic and only pass when it is necessary and safe to do so.

question: What best ensures your safety when preparing to back up your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors only.,b:Open the door and look behind as you back up.,c:Honk immediately before shifting into reverse.,d:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check behind it before getting in.
note: Backing requires extra caution. Before getting in to back up, walk behind the vehicle to check for children or small obstacles, and while backing turn your head to look through the rear window rather than relying only on mirrors.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling in the same direction?
options: a:Wait until no oncoming traffic, then pass with sufficient space.,b:Continue driving straight and expect the bicyclist to move.,c:Do not pass until a signalized intersection.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles, leaving at least 3 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds) and not passing too fast or close.

question: Is it beneficial to continually improve your driving and observation skills because driving always involves some risk?
options: a:No — improvement is unnecessary.,b:Yes — continually improving driving and observation is wise.,c:Only required for new drivers.,d:Only necessary if you drive in bad weather.
note: Because driving always involves risk, drivers should continually work to improve their driving and observation skills for safety.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Decreases your field of vision.,b:Increases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:Has no effect.
note: As speed increases your field of vision narrows, reducing your ability to detect hazards. Drive more cautiously at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit or safe place to turn around.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder.,c:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
note: If you miss an exit, keep going to the next exit; never back up or attempt an abrupt lane change on a freeway.

question: When may you cross a broken (dashed) white line?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:At any time.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

question: Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk. Is the statement \Drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk\" true or false?"
options: a:True — drivers need not stop.,b:False — drivers must stop and yield.,c:Only true at night.,d:Only true on multilane roads.
note: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on the driver’s side when no traffic control signals are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal displays a red light and a green arrow pointing your way, may you turn in the arrow's direction?
options: a:True — after yielding to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.,b:False
note: A green arrow allows you to proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to any conflicting traffic or pedestrians in the intersection.

question: A pennant-shaped roadside sign typically means:
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs on the left side of the road are used to mark the beginning of a no-passing zone.

question: If you are nervous, angry, or upset before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before driving.,b:You will drive the same as when calm.,c:Drive faster because you are more alert.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and impair driving; calm yourself and regain focus before getting behind the wheel.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:If you are turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward/away from a curb (all of the above),b:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Turning left or right.,d:Changing lanes.
note: Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder whenever you change your vehicle's position—turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

question: Upon hearing a siren or seeing flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what is required?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you on the left.,d:Continue through the intersection and then stop.
note: Yield the right-of-way by driving to the right side of the road and stopping until the emergency vehicle has passed; if in an intersection, clear it first before stopping.

question: Hydroplaning is most commonly caused by which factor?
options: a:Excessive stops.,b:Sudden turns.,c:Driving too fast for wet road conditions.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot clear water at higher speeds and begin to ride on a film of water, causing loss of traction.

question: Which distraction increases the risk of a crash the most?
options: a:Listening to a CD player.,b:Changing radio stations.,c:Using a cell phone (even hands-free).,d:Adjusting the climate controls.
note: Using a cell phone, including hands-free devices, is a major distraction and increases crash risk more than ordinary in-car tasks.

question: If your turn signals are not working, which method should you use to show your intention to turn?
options: a:Use your headlights.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Use hand signals to indicate your turn.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and leave them on.
note: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, use the standard hand signals to show other road users when you intend to turn or change lanes.

question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The arrow is never used,b:The same as a circular red light—you must stop and may not turn in that direction,c:Drivers may turn in the arrow's direction,d:The arrow only applies to pedestrians
note: A solid red arrow requires traffic facing the arrow to stop and prohibits turning in the indicated direction until the signal changes.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; scan traffic in both directions and enter the intersection carefully.

question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,c:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
note: Large trucks may travel much slower on steep grades; exercise caution and do not pass on hills or where visibility is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs state the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speeds under ideal conditions; drivers must reduce speed when conditions warrant.

question: If a train is approaching and poses a danger, what must you do at the railroad crossing?
options: a:Proceed slowly with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross if there are no lights or gates.,d:Stop briefly and then cross quickly.
note: If a train is close enough or traveling fast enough to pose a risk, you must not cross the tracks until it has passed completely, even without signals.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, what should you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Drive with your flashers turned on.,c:Speed up and leave the street.
note: On a one-way street, when an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, pull to the nearest curb or roadside and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Does a double solid yellow centerline allow passing from either direction?
options: a:False — passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:True
note: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate no passing by traffic from either direction.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Traffic volume is greater at night.,b:Drivers generally drive faster at night.,c:Reduced visibility—drivers cannot see as well in the dark.,d:Vehicles are less reliable at night.
note: Because visibility is reduced at night, headlights must be used and drivers should exercise greater caution between half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Expect the right-of-way and force entry.,b:Yield to vehicles already on the public road.,c:Always stop and wait for a police officer.,d:Drive quickly to merge into traffic.
note: When entering from a driveway or private road, yield to traffic already on the public roadway and merge safely when there is a gap.

question: Which practice helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,c:Add extra weight to improve traction.
note: Reducing speed and increasing the space between vehicles are the primary techniques to reduce crash risk on slippery roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an unmarked stop sign or where no crosswalk exists, where must you stop?
options: a:Before entering the intersection.,b:Only if other cars are present.,c:Before the crosswalk even if none exists.,d:You do not need to stop.
note: At a stop sign, stop at the stop line; if none, stop before entering the intersection. If a crosswalk exists, stop before it.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, which action is recommended?
options: a:Try to steer straight and gradually slow by lifting off the gas; do not brake hard immediately.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Maintain speed and steer straight.
note: On a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, avoid sudden braking until under control, then pull off safely.

question: When faced with an aggressive driver, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,b:Cut them off to teach them a lesson.,c:Retaliate by tailgating.,d:Make obscene gestures to intimidate them.
note: Avoid confrontation—do not make eye contact, slow down, and let an aggressive driver pass to reduce danger.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Flash your lights.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: Always slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians, especially near schools, driveways, and crosswalks; yield the right-of-way when required.

question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?
options: a:Increase stopping distance and risk of hydroplaning; make turning more difficult.,b:Make turning easier.,c:Have no effect on braking.
note: Worn tires reduce traction, lengthen stopping distance, increase hydroplaning risk, and make handling worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to other drivers when:
options: a:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.,b:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,c:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
note: You must yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley.

question: May you stop or park on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:As long as you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in an emergency; stopping for convenience is not allowed.

question: Is it illegal to crowd a motorcycle by trying to share its lane?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a lane; it is illegal and unsafe for a car to try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal your intention to turn?
options: a:50 feet.,b:10 feet.,c:100 feet.,d:200 feet.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before making a turn or lane change to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: Which safety restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Both lap/shoulder belt and airbag used together.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Only a lap and shoulder belt.
note: Wearing both a properly adjusted lap/shoulder belt and having an airbag provides the best protection in frontal crashes.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Either side of the road,b:The center,c:The right side of the road.
note: If another vehicle's high beams are blinding you, glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded until the vehicle passes.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road signify?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is allowed.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; a solid white line indicates lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.

question: Which of these places is parking prohibited?
options: a:In front of mailboxes.,b:Within a highway tunnel.,c:On bridges.
note: Parking is prohibited in numerous locations including in front of driveways, in tunnels, and on bridges; follow posted signs and local laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow centerline, what does that indicate?
options: a:Traffic flows in both directions.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates two-way traffic and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When emergency vehicles are approaching with flashing lights or sirens, pull to the side and make a clear path if it is safe to do so.

question: What is a frequent cause of many crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for the conditions.,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,c:Yielding the right-of-way.
note: Many crashes result from drivers traveling too fast for the conditions; adjust speed to match road, weather, and traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection of two similar roads with no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the left.,b:The car in which the driver sounds the horn first.,c:The car approaching from the right.,d:The car that arrived second.
note: At intersections without control devices, a driver must yield to vehicles approaching from the right.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your low beam headlights?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Use low beams (or fog lights if available) in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey the displayed instruction are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs
note: Regulatory signs must be obeyed; failure to comply with these signs can result in penalties.

question: Which of the following statements about work zones is correct?
options: a:They are marked with black and white signs.,b:They may be moving or stationary.,c:They never require drivers to slow down.,d:They always close the road.
note: Work zones can be stationary (construction area) or moving (mowing, line striping). They are typically marked by orange signs and drivers should slow down and pay extra attention.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Stop completely, then proceed when safe.,b:Drive through if no crossing traffic.,c:Continue since you have right-of-way.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: come to a full stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

question: When driving on major highways, which practice is important?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving and be ready to react to hazards.,b:Stare straight ahead to maintain focus.,c:Relax and let cruise control handle hazards.
note: Stay alert, scan frequently, and be prepared to respond to changing road or traffic conditions to avoid 'highway hypnosis'.

question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low-beam headlights in rainy conditions to improve visibility and avoid glare reflected by water on the road.

question: A single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not permitted.,d:Separates a bicycle lane from traffic
note: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; drivers next to the broken line may pass when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after those ahead have gone, what must you do?
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:May slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must come to a complete stop at the stop sign; do not roll through because other traffic pressures suggest you skip the stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, yield to the vehicle on your right if you arrive simultaneously; proceed only when it is safe.

question: What primarily affects your ability to stop?
options: a:Road conditions such as wet, icy, or uneven pavement.,b:Signal lights.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping ability is most affected by road surface conditions; reduce speed on slippery or poor pavement to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield just to the traffic on the right.,b:Always stop before entering the intersection.,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians in the roadway you are entering.
note: A yield sign means slow down and yield to vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection or road you are entering; stop if necessary.

question: A person carrying a white cane or using a guide dog most likely is:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A deaf person.,c:A participant in a traffic study.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to blind pedestrians who use a white cane or guide dog.

question: How can you avoid becoming drowsy on a long trip?
options: a:Stop at regular intervals to rest.,b:Turn on your car radio.,c:Slow down.
note: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, schedule frequent stops to rest, stretch, and refresh even before feeling tired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'No stopping' sign allows you to stop only in which situation?
options: a:Long enough to unload packages.,b:To discharge passengers.,c:To avoid conflict with other traffic.
note: A No Stopping sign means you may not stop except to obey a traffic signal or a police officer, or to prevent a conflict with other traffic.

question: If sleet or snow begins while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.,b:Allow additional distance between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead.,c:Approach all vehicles with caution.,d:All of the above
note: In snowy or icy conditions, clear vision, increased following distance, and cautious approach to other vehicles help reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk marked, where should you stop?
options: a:You are not required to stop.,b:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,c:In the middle of the intersecting roadway so you can see traffic from both directions.,d:Wherever you want as long as you slow down.
note: When there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest to the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of oncoming traffic without entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in the roadway waiting to complete a left turn, how should you position your steering wheel?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to warn others.,d:Turn the wheel sharply when the opportunity arises.
note: Keep your wheels pointed straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision will not push you into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does vehicle speed affect the distance you travel after applying the brakes?
options: a:False — higher speed increases stopping distance.,b:True
note: Speed greatly affects stopping distance; the faster you travel, the longer it takes to stop due to increased reaction and braking distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a correct passing procedure?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,b:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.,c:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.
note: When passing, signal in advance (at least 100 feet in residential areas), check mirrors and blind spots, and return only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,b:One driver should continue driving without stopping.,c:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if two vehicles arrive together, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing where there is no traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:The driver,c:Whoever is slower.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the roadway, even when making turns and even if no signal is present.

question: Should drivers avoid staying beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:True — large blind spots make it unsafe.,b:False
note: Large vehicles have extensive blind spots; avoid driving alongside them for long durations by moving ahead or falling back.

question: What does an orange-colored traffic sign indicate?
options: a:A no-passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance work ahead.,c:A school zone.,d:A regulatory speed sign.
note: Orange signs indicate construction, maintenance, and emergency operations; drive with extra caution in these areas.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Go through the intersection.,b:Yield to other cars but continue.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop because it will change to red.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red; slow and prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating the vehicle travels 25 mph or less; use caution around these vehicles.

question: What does a diamond-shaped roadway sign typically indicate?
options: a:A lane assignment sign.,b:A warning of a hazard or special condition ahead.,c:A route marker for interstates.,d:A regulatory instruction such as Stop or Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to hazards or unusual conditions ahead; in work areas they are often orange.

question: Where and when should you slow down while driving?
options: a:Only in residential neighborhoods.,b:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings, and when the road is wet or slippery.,c:Only when police are present.,d:Only when following a bus.
note: Reduce speed on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in blind curves, around pedestrians, and when surfaces are slippery.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, what should you do when pedestrians are in the crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.,b:When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.,c:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
note: Marked crosswalks indicate where pedestrians should cross; you must yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

question: What color are guide signs that provide directions and mileage information?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green,d:Blue
note: Guide (destination) signs are green and provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Never — you have the right-of-way.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:Whenever you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren, you must yield.,d:Only on city streets.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using its siren or flashing lights, regardless of location.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn you must do what to your speed?
options: a:Maintain your speed.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Vary (reduce) your speed to maintain control.
note: Reduce speed as needed to maintain control and stay in your lane while turning; avoid accelerating until you are clear of the turn.

question: If you need to slow on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: First remove your foot from the accelerator to allow your vehicle to slow; apply brakes gently if additional slowing is needed.

question: What does a 'No standing' sign allow you to do at that location?
options: a:You may park there if you remain in the vehicle.,b:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or drop off passengers.,c:You may never stop your vehicle there.,d:You may stop to load or unload cargo.
note: A 'No standing' sign means you may only stop temporarily to load or unload passengers; you may not park and wait.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.
note: Do not make sudden or illegal maneuvers; proceed to the next exit and safely re-route to your destination.

question: Should motorists maintain a safe operating distance when near a cyclist?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Give cyclists ample space and be especially careful when passing or turning near them.

question: If you are in an accident and another person is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Move injured persons immediately away from the scene.,b:Leave injured persons where they are and avoid helping.,c:Do not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if qualified.,d:Always move the injured into your vehicle to transport them.
note: Do not move injured people unnecessarily as improper handling can worsen injuries; keep them warm and provide appropriate first aid until professionals arrive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are not working due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.,b:Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.,c:Yield to other drivers in the same manner as at a four-way stop and proceed when it is safe.
note: When signals are out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop: stop, yield as appropriate, and proceed with caution when it is your turn.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Yellow and white,d:Blue
note: Yellow center lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when you see a police officer.,b:When anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.,c:Only while entering a highway.,d:Never—always obey the posted limit.
note: Even when driving within the posted limit, you must reduce speed when weather, visibility, road surface, or traffic make the posted speed unsafe.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
options: a:15 feet,b:50 feet,c:25 feet,d:40 feet
note: Minnesota law prohibits parking within 50 feet of a railroad crossing so that drivers approaching the crossing can see clearly.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads; it can reduce your control when traction is lost.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn on multilane one-way streets and highways?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street, position your vehicle in the leftmost lane for that direction before turning.

question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue driving when they think most kids are done exiting the bus.
note: Stop when a school bus displays stop signals; remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and it is safe to proceed.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It harms both driving skills and judgement.,b:It helps driving skills but harms judgement.,c:It has no effect.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, judgment, and increases risky behaviors, reducing driving safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to an intersection showing a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,b:Stop only if other cars are nearby.,c:Come to a full stop, yield, and proceed when safe.,d:Proceed since it is only a caution signal.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and go only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Only check your side mirror.,b:Signal after starting your lane change.,c:Check your side and rearview mirrors, signal, and verify other drivers are not moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, use your signal, and ensure the lane is clear.

question: About how much distance might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop when traveling at 55 mph?
options: a:400 feet.,b:125 feet.,c:50 feet.,d:200 feet.
note: Large tractor-trailers require much greater stopping distances than passenger vehicles. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need nearly 400 feet to stop from 55 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does increasing vehicle speed make it take longer to stop when reacting to unexpected movements?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Higher speeds increase reaction and braking distances, so the faster you go the longer it will take to stop for hazards.

question: How should drivers treat bicycles on the road?
options: a:They must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.,b:They are nothing to worry about.,c:They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles are vehicles under the law and motorists must respect bicyclists' rights and follow the same general rules.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:If flashing red lights are activated, if a crossing gate is lowered, or if a stop sign is posted.,b:Only if you see a train nearby.,c:Only if the crossing lights are flashing.
note: You must stop at crossings when lights flash, gates are down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger indicates to stop, or if a train is visible and too close to cross safely.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red, what should you do?
options: a:Honk your horn to warn them.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians even if you have a green light; they have the right-of-way in the crosswalk.

question: Only vehicles displaying special plates or disabled parking placards may use spaces reserved for persons with disabilities.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking spaces marked by a Reserved Parking for Persons with Disabilities sign may only be used by vehicles displaying the appropriate plates or placards.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best option?
options: a:Stop driving and rest.,b:Open your window, c:Get some coffee.
note: If you feel tired, pull over safely and rest; temporary measures like coffee may not prevent drowsiness and are not reliable.

question: If another vehicle is in danger of hitting you, what should you do?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Turn on your emergency lights.,c:Sound your horn to warn them.,d:Swerve into oncoming traffic.
note: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians when you believe they may not see you and a collision is possible.

question: Which of the following is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Talking or texting on a cell phone.,b:Changing a radio station or CD.,c:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,d:Any of the above.
note: Distracted driving can be caused by many activities, including using a cell phone, eating, drinking, smoking, or adjusting audio devices. Any non-driving task can be dangerous.

question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Slow down when roads are wet and maintain tires in good condition.,b:Keep cruise control engaged on wet roads.,c:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions, avoid standing water, and keep tires properly maintained to lower hydroplaning risk.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what should other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,c:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Heavy trucks require more distance to stop; other drivers should leave extra space and avoid lingering in a truck's blind spots.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.,c:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
note: At rail intersections, obey all traffic signals and signs, and look both ways before turning across tracks; never drive around lowered gates.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:It is more likely to be raining at night.
note: Night driving reduces your field of vision and makes it harder to detect hazards; use appropriate headlights and reduce speed.

question: If a vehicle hydroplanes and starts to skid, should you apply the brakes quickly?
options: a:False — do not immediately apply brakes; release accelerator and steer to regain control.,b:True
note: If hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator, steer straight or toward the skid to regain control, and avoid immediate hard braking.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:Prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
note: A space cushion gives you time to perceive and react to hazards, reducing the chance of collisions.

question: When is it permissible to text while driving?
options: a:If the driver can send the text without looking at their phone.,b:At any time when the driver is under age 18.,c:Only in an emergency.,d:At any time when the driver is age 18 or older.
note: Drivers may not use a mobile device for text messaging while driving except in an emergency. Any distraction that takes your eyes or attention from the road increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on a highway with two solid yellow center lines, which is allowed?
options: a:You may cross the lines to pass other vehicles, but only if there is no oncoming traffic.,b:You may cross these lines under no circumstances.,c:You may cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
note: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of the roadway where passing is prohibited; you may only cross them to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

question: If the centerline has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:Never.,c:When traffic is clear and it is safe to pass.,d:Only on an expressway.
note: When the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may proceed carefully through an intersection with a yellow light under which condition?
options: a:There are pedestrians crossing.,b:You are already within the intersection.,c:You are turning right.
note: If a steady yellow light appears and you are already within the intersection, proceed carefully; otherwise, prepare to stop.

question: What is the proper top-to-bottom order of colors on a vertical traffic light?
options: a:Green, red, yellow.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Red, yellow, green.
note: On a vertical signal, red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: Which actions should you take when driving in fog?
options: a:Drive cautiously at reduced speeds, do not use high beams, and use low beams.,b:Use high beam headlights to see farther.,c:Use only parking lights.
note: In fog reduce speed, use low beams (and fog lights if available) because high beams worsen visibility by reflecting off fog.

question: What can happen when alcohol is consumed with drugs?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased, making driving more dangerous.,b:The effects are decreased.,c:It helps cure your illness.
note: Combining alcohol and drugs can amplify impairment and significantly increase the danger of driving.

question: The space needed to cross traffic depends on which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:The presence of a stop sign.,c:Whether you used your turn signal.
note: The space required to cross traffic depends on pavement and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine or other emergency vehicle behind you, what action must you take?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or sirens, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: After being stopped by law enforcement, should a driver immediately exit the vehicle and approach the officer’s squad car?
options: a:Yes — exit quickly to speak to the officer.,b:No — remain in your vehicle with hands visible.,c:Only if the officer asks you to do so.,d:Yes, unless it is raining.
note: If stopped, stay in your vehicle and keep your hands in plain sight on the steering wheel unless the officer instructs otherwise.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle with blinding high beams, what should you do?
options: a:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,b:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.,c:Glance toward the right side of the road and the edge of your lane until the vehicle passes.,d:Dim your lights and accelerate to pass quickly.
note: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams, avoid looking directly at the lights. Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle has passed to avoid being blinded.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon.,b:Rectangle.,c:Square.,d:Circle.
note: A stop sign has an octagonal shape. The eight-sided shape is used only for stop signs to make them recognizable even if partially obscured.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is accurate?
options: a:They can stay alert by opening windows and turning up the radio.,b:They may drive so poorly they resemble drunk drivers.,c:Drinking strong coffee eliminates drowsiness.,d:They usually drive better at night.
note: Drowsy drivers can exhibit driving behaviors similar to intoxicated drivers; opening a window or radio often does not restore adequate alertness.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and are entitled to the full width of a lane; never try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: Should drivers use high beam headlights when driving in fog to increase their field of vision?
options: a:True,b:False
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; use low beams or fog lights instead if driving in fog is necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has more than one lane in your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The lane closest to the lane you came from.,b:The middle lane regardless of where you came from.,c:The furthest lane to the left.,d:Any lane as long as you signal.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane street, turn into the lane nearest to the one you were in and avoid changing lanes during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To turn into or from a driveway or to make a left turn where permitted.,c:To pass another car.,d:Never under any condition.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing, but you may cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where allowed.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually to avoid unnecessary braking.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.
note: Anticipating traffic and slowing gradually reduces frequent acceleration and improves fuel economy.

question: What do double solid yellow center lines mean?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Railroad crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and prohibit passing from either direction, except for permitted left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, what checks are required?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots before signaling and changing lanes.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Always check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before passing; re-enter when the passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.

question: On average, how much alcohol does the body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three drinks per hour.,b:One standard drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:No alcohol is eliminated for several hours.
note: On average, the body metabolizes about one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: Highway signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions and should be obeyed to reduce crash risk.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment and increase the risk of dangerous side effects and loss of control.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways under normal conditions.,c:When driving only during the day.,d:When traveling downhill with good traction.
note: Stopping distances are longer on wet, icy, loose gravel, or otherwise slippery surfaces, so increase following distance accordingly.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle with sirens and lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights or sirens approaches, you must immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic,c:After you have stopped at least 20 feet prior to the intersection.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which method is the correct way to check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the outside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head to check the blind spot before moving.,c:Using the inside rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder toward the direction of your move to ensure the blind spot is clear.

question: How is distracted driving characterized?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that greatly increases crash risk.,b:Very uncommon.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving dramatically increases the chance of crashes; keep attention focused on driving at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red and white triangular yield sign mean at an intersection?
options: a:Slow and yield the right-of-way; be prepared to stop if necessary.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A yield sign means reduce speed and give the right-of-way to vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection; stop if required.

question: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move over to provide space or slow down if lane change is unsafe.,b:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,c:Drive to the right and stop completely.
note: If possible, change lanes away from the stopped emergency, tow, or service vehicle; if unsafe, slow below the posted limit and give extra space.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is generally:
options: a:More dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:Less dangerous.,d:Always safer because of fewer cars.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous due to reduced visibility, glare from lights, and a higher likelihood of tired or impaired drivers on the road.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you to the possibility of a train; be prepared to stop and obey crossing signals and gates.

question: When you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Drive as far right as safely possible and stop,c:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass,d:Speed up to get out of its way
note: On two-lane roadways, immediately drive as near as possible to the right side and stop, taking care not to stop in an intersection, so the emergency vehicle can pass.

question: What helps you avoid emergency stops when driving in traffic?
options: a:Constantly honking to alert others.,b:Looking ahead and maintaining a safe following distance.,c:Staying strictly in the right lane.,d:Driving faster than surrounding traffic.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead gives you time to react without needing abrupt emergency stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection and the light changes from green to solid yellow, you should:
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and always continue through.,b:Stop immediately no matter how close you are to the intersection.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A solid yellow warns that the light is about to turn red—stop before entering if you can do so safely; otherwise clear the intersection carefully.

question: When riding in a vehicle, what is true about small children?
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult.,b:Must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint for their size and age.,c:Will be safe if standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
note: Children must be restrained in properly sized child safety seats or booster seats until they are large enough for regular seat belts to fit properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which speed?
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions, not exceeding posted limits.,b:The maximum speed limit only.,c:A speed that is safe for existing conditions only.
note: You must always drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for road, traffic, weather, and visibility conditions, within legal limits.

question: A diamond-shaped warning sign tells drivers:
options: a:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,b:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,c:Alerts drivers to school zones.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn of potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

question: Must a motorist making a left turn yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
options: a:True — yield to oncoming bicycles like any other vehicle.,b:False
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would yield to oncoming motor vehicles.

question: The color orange on signs usually indicates:
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Orange signs typically warn drivers about construction or work zones; many are diamond-shaped and highly visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit to complete a pass on roads with speed limits under 55 mph?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not exceed the posted speed limit to complete a pass on roadways where the speed limit is under 55 mph; only where permitted by law and posted allow higher actions.

question: After an upsetting incident at work, what is the safest action before driving home?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself.,b:Drive fast to release emotions.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.,d:Call a friend while driving to vent.
note: If you are upset or distracted, take time to cool off before driving; emotional distraction impairs judgment and increases crash risk.

question: Which effects are commonly caused by alcohol?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol impairs concentration, coordination, and judgment even in small amounts, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, where should you complete the turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Either lane.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, turn into the lane closest to your previous lane, unless signs or markings indicate otherwise.

question: You must come to a stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:Steady yellow light.,b:Yellow arrow.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red signal means stop; treat it like a stop sign, then proceed when it is safe.

question: Which of the following does NOT help promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.,c:Install heavy window tinting that reduces nighttime visibility.,d:Use low-beam headlights in poor visibility.
note: Anything that reduces visibility (for example, very dark window tinting) does not promote safe night driving. Keep windows clean, use proper headlights, and carry a flashlight if needed.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, what should you do while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window,b:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach,d:Exit your vehicle and walk to the officer
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the wheel, ask passengers to keep hands in view, and wait for the officer to request your license and documents.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply say no if offered a drink, then drive.,c:Call a taxi only after you've been drinking heavily.
note: The safest approach is to plan not to drive before you start drinking; don't rely on decisions made after drinking when judgement is impaired.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop.,b:Only slow if you see flashing lights.,c:Always change gears before crossing tracks.
note: Slow, look and listen for trains; if gates are down or lights are flashing, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks and do not attempt to go around barriers.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,b:Slow and drive through if clear.,c:Stop only if a police officer is present.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop completely, then go when the intersection is clear.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving more slowly than traffic.,c:Always making quick and sudden stops.
note: Drunk drivers often weave, speed, make sudden braking or turning maneuvers, and generally have impaired vehicle control.

question: Is liability insurance required for every motor vehicle in Minnesota?
options: a:True — every motor vehicle must be covered by liability insurance.,b:False — insurance is optional.,c:Only required for commercial vehicles.,d:Only required for vehicles older than 10 years.
note: Minnesota law requires valid liability insurance on every motor vehicle and proof of insurance must be carried when driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,c:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
note: You must stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and make the stop before crossing the sidewalk area.

question: A flashing red traffic signal should be treated the same as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.,d:A no-passing sign.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a full stop and yield before proceeding.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:To keep the front wheels straight.
note: If your vehicle skids, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go (often 'into' the skid) and then straighten the wheel as control returns.

question: Which of these can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication, including over-the-counter drugs.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:None of the above.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, illegal and legal drugs (including some over-the-counter medications), and fatigue. Always check medication labels and warnings before driving.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may not turn and must proceed straight.,c:You have exclusive right-of-way to turn.,d:You must stop and wait for a green arrow.
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, you may still turn in that direction but must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: What is the correct use of a freeway exit ramp regarding braking?
options: a:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,b:Maintain speed until you are on the exit ramp, then slow down.,c:Keep constant speed once on the exit ramp.,d:Stop at the start of the exit ramp and then coast down.
note: Do not slow down on the mainline before the exit; slow down once you are on the exit ramp at the appropriate deceleration area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If someone drives much slower than the speed limit and causes a backup, what is required?
options: a:They should pull off the road and let following cars pass when safe.,b:They always have the right of way.,c:They are the safest drivers.
note: Drivers who impede traffic by going much slower should pull over when safe to allow others to pass.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Using a cell phone or other electronic device while driving distracts you from the task and increases crash risk; only use to report emergencies if necessary.

question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed management when driving through curves?
options: a:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Drive at the posted speed and then brake at the sharpest part.,d:Increase speed while in the curve to maintain momentum.
note: Because inertia can push your vehicle outward in a curve, reduce your speed before entering the curve so you can maintain control throughout.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Watch carefully for children walking along the roadside and proceed only when clear.,b:Proceed once children wave to you.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the bus area.
note: After a bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children along the road and proceed cautiously only when safe.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:Amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and time between drinks.,b:Only how much you enjoy the beverage.,c:Whether you are driving before drinking.
note: BAC is influenced by how much you drink, how quickly, body weight, and food in the stomach which slows absorption.

question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must pull over and allow it to pass:
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of its direction, you must pull to the right edge of the road and stop.,d:Only on highways.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights or siren by pulling over to the right and stopping, no matter the direction from which they come.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which maneuver is allowed from a center left-turn lane?
options: a:You may pass slow-moving traffic.,b:You may make left turns.,c:You may make U-turns.
note: A center left-turn lane is for vehicles making left turns from either direction; it is not for passing or through traffic.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:The person driving the car.,b:Passengers only on long trips.,c:All occupants of the vehicle.,d:Only occupants in the front seats.
note: Make sure every person in the vehicle wears a seat belt—unrestrained occupants can be seriously injured and become hazards to others in a crash.

question: Which of the following will help a person sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee,b:Tomato juice and lime,c:Fresh air,d:Allowing enough time to pass
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; remedies such as coffee, fresh air, or food do not sober you up.

question: What does a flashing yellow X lane-use signal mean?
options: a:This lane may be used only for left turns.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
note: A flashing yellow X indicates the lane is only for left turns; obey lane control signals to avoid conflicts.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to allow them to pass.
note: If someone is following too closely, slow down and, when safe, move over to let them pass; do not brake-check or escalate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely through it without stopping; blocking intersections is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm extended upward signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to turn left.,c:The driver is coming to a stop.
note: A left arm extended upward is the hand signal indicating a right turn; know hand signals in case lights fail.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large trucks and buses have extensive no-zones, including far behind the vehicle; avoid following too closely.

question: What describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who daydreams or stares off the roadway while driving.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger.,c:Someone who only watches the vehicle ahead.
note: An inattentive driver is distracted by sights or thoughts off the road, increasing crash risk; maintain scanning and attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding can be fatal.,c:Speeding is not dangerous for skilled drivers.,d:Both A and B
note: Both driving much slower than traffic and speeding create hazards; higher speeds greatly increase the chance of fatal crashes.

question: What does an advisory speed sign attached to a curve sign indicate?
options: a:A recommended speed for the curve that should be reduced further in poor conditions.,b:A sign that may be ignored in rain or snow.,c:A blue sign with black lettering.
note: Advisory speed plaques recommend a safe speed for curves; in adverse weather you should reduce speed even more.

question: What do fluorescent yellow-green traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning areas.,b:Hospitals ahead.,c:Speed limits.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green is used for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning signs; be extra cautious near these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off to the right and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Refuse to let other cars pass.
note: When driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic and causing a backup on a two-lane, two-way road, pull off the road when safe to allow others to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive in a lane displaying a red X lane-use signal?
options: a:If you are passing the car in front of you.,b:If there is no visible oncoming traffic.,c:Never.
note: A red X over a lane means the lane is closed to traffic; you must not drive in it.

question: A double solid yellow line at the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction.

question: What should drivers do to following distance when driving in bad weather?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Maintain the normal following distance.,d:Follow as close as possible to help other drivers.
note: In adverse weather or poor visibility, increase your following distance so you have more time to react and stop if needed.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, what must you do?
