options: a:Slow down but remain in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane and ignore it.,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: You must immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Sound your horn and continue driving.,d:Turn off the ignition (without locking the steering), apply the brakes, and move safely off the road.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral if possible, turn off the ignition carefully so you do not lock the steering, apply the brakes, and steer the vehicle off the road to a safe location.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,d:Stop and flash your lights.
note: On narrow roads you must allow vehicles traveling in the opposite direction at least one-half of the main-traveled portion so both can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal requires you to come to a full stop, yield, and then proceed when clear?
options: a:A solid green light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.,d:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means the same as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to others, then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the interstate.,b:Continue to the next exit and safely return.,c:Back up in your lane to reach the exit.,d:Signal and cross the median to return to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, do not back up or turn around on the highway; go to the next exit and return safely.

question: Is it legal to drive through, around, or under a railroad crossing gate or barrier?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never drive around or under lowered railroad gates or barriers; it is illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow signal, how should you respond?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving, as you have the right-of-way.,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already within the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon be red; stop safely unless you are already in the intersection.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light indicates you should slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: Which is NOT a primary factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Braking distance,b:Reaction distance,c:Steering ability.
note: Stopping distance depends mainly on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a primary factor in the stopping distance calculation.

question: When a traffic signal light turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,b:Back up slowly.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must first yield to any pedestrians or traffic still in the intersection.

question: Before backing up, what should you do?
options: a:Check behind your vehicle before getting in and use mirrors and look back while backing.,b:Depend entirely on your mirrors.,c:Accelerate quickly when backing up.
note: Always check behind your vehicle for children or objects before entering and use mirrors and direct observation while reversing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, which driver must yield?
options: a:Either driver may proceed.,b:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,c:The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.,d:The larger vehicle must yield.
note: At intersections where drivers arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: Which action reduces the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving through shallow water.,b:Driving more slowly.,c:Driving more quickly.
note: Hydroplaning is more likely when driving too fast on wet surfaces; reduce speed to lower the risk.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Driving too fast for conditions.,c:Following too closely.,d:All of the above.
note: Common causes of crashes include inattention, excessive speed for conditions, and tailgating, among other factors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are hand and arm signals permitted instead of mechanical turn signals?
options: a:At night,b:During daylight hours,c:When driving a loaded vehicle that blocks hand signals,d:When passing on a two-lane road
note: Hand and arm signals may be used during the day in addition to or instead of mechanical signals; do not use hand signals at night or when they are not visible.

question: What do your brake lights signal to other drivers?
options: a:Are making a turn.,b:Are slowing down or stopping.,c:Are changing lanes.
note: Brake lights alert following drivers that you are slowing or stopping; keep them in working order.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition.,b:The time of day only.,c:Presence of signal lights only.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, vehicle mechanical condition (brakes/tires), and roadway surface condition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in an urban or town area is:
options: a:45 mph.,b:30 mph.,c:55 mph.
note: In urban or town areas, the default speed limit is typically 30 miles per hour unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are drivers required to stop their vehicles?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:Only when a traffic officer orders a stop.
note: You must stop at stop signs, when a red light is shown, or whenever a traffic officer instructs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside, which action is required?
options: a:Vacate the nearest lane or slow down if you cannot safely move over.,b:Increase your speed to get past quickly.,c:Pull off behind the stopped vehicle and wait.
note: The Move Over Law requires drivers to move over one lane for stopped emergency, tow, sanitation, and utility vehicles; if unsafe, slow down and pass with care.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,d:Always travel slower uphill
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:Night drives.,c:High speeds.
note: Higher speeds increase the distance required to stop and the force of impact in a crash, making injuries more severe.

question: A sign stating 'Reduced speed 35 mph' means what?
options: a:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,b:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,c:That you have plenty of time to slow before the reduced speed zone.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new speed limit begins at the sign unless otherwise indicated.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe; those next to the solid line may not.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.,b:By looking in your side mirrors.,c:By looking in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors alone; glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes or merging.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:False — you must never share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:True
note: Motorcycles require a full lane; never drive side-by-side in the same lane as a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even if no traffic is visible.,b:Only signal if other traffic is present.,c:Only signal at night.,d:Signal only when turning right.
note: Always use your signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb to properly communicate your intent.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite flows of traffic and indicates passing is allowed when it can be done safely.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can occur?
options: a:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can be cited for violating traffic laws.

question: What is the purpose of highway markings?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Are only found in construction zones.,c:Provide information for drivers.
note: Pavement markings guide lane placement, passing zones, and warn of upcoming conditions; obey them for safe operation.

question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, what must you do?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Yield the right-of-way to disabled pedestrians who use assistive devices; they are entitled to the same protections as all pedestrians.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow indicate?
options: a:Arrows are never used,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light—you must prepare to stop,c:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow,d:It applies only to buses
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turn phase is ending; slow down and prepare to stop because the signal is about to turn red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection together, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.,c:The car on the right must yield.,d:The vehicle with the highest speed must yield.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Let it go.,b:Pull up alongside and yell at them.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.,d:Follow them closely to teach them a lesson.
note: Avoid road rage and retaliation—stay calm, give extra space if needed, and continue driving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Check your mirrors and blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Check your rearview and side mirrors and also glance over your shoulder to be sure no one is in your blind spot before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic on the highway and merge when safe.,b:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp, then slowly enter traffic.,d:Drive on the shoulder to enter traffic.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed, signal, look for an opening, and merge into traffic when it is safe to do so.

question: At night, which is hardest to see?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Road signs.,c:Pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians are often the hardest to see at night compared with signs or other vehicles; be especially vigilant.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, which documents must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of insurance only.,b:Driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.,c:Proof of registration only.,d:Only their driver's license and insurance card.
note: When stopped, drivers must present their license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance upon request.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you first look carefully in both directions.,d:As long as an approaching train is not too close.
note: Flashing lights, lowered gates, or bells at a railroad crossing require you to stop; do not go around or under a moving or lowered gate.

question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,c:Take your eyes off the road.
note: Distractions that take your eyes, hands, or attention away from driving increase crash risk.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:Run out into the street without looking,d:Always stay on the sidewalk.
note: Reduce speed and be prepared for unpredictable actions by children; they may run into the street without warning.

question: When roads may be slippery, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Reduce your following distance.
note: On slippery roads, reduce your speed and increase your following distance; do not use cruise control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do you have to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must use your turn signal any time you pull away from a curb to indicate your intentions to other drivers and pedestrians.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign usually warns of what?
options: a:A no-passing zone ahead.,b:A school zone or school crossing.,c:A speed limit change.,d:A railroad crossing.
note: Pentagonal signs are used to indicate school zones and school crossings—be alert for children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action when approaching a roundabout?
options: a:Decrease your speed and be prepared to yield.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Increase your speed to enter quickly.
note: Approach a roundabout at a slow speed, yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians, and enter when safe.

question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,d:How much you drink.
note: BAC depends on weight, amount consumed, and time between drinks; the beverage type does not directly affect BAC.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and nearby road work.,b:That it is summer.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Work zone signs are typically orange and warn that workers or equipment are on or near the roadway; slow down and use extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm and hand extended downward signal?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Stop or slow down.
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver intends to stop or slow; be prepared to slow or stop behind them.

question: Which winter driving statement is not true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels frequently in winter.
note: Using cruise control in winter conditions is unsafe; winter driving requires extra caution and proper vehicle maintenance.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is on your side of the road.,b:Only if you see children crossing.,c:When the bus's red lights are flashing and it is stopped to load or unload children.,d:Never, if you are in a vehicle with seat belts.
note: On a two-lane road, all traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while stopped to load or unload children.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Four-way hazard flashers.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Headlights (low beams) when appropriate.,d:No lights are necessary.
note: Turn on headlights at dusk or on overcast days; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: If a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a private road, must you stop?
options: a:True — you must stop.,b:False
note: Drivers must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing regardless of whether the road is public or private.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn as a warning when it may prevent a collision, for example to alert a child who appears about to run into the street.

question: Which of the following is important to remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:The road is most slippery just after it starts to rain.,b:Hydroplaning cannot occur if you reduce speed.,c:You need no extra space when stopping.,d:Stand on the brakes to drive through puddles.
note: Road surfaces are especially slippery right after rain begins due to oils and grime; reduce speed and increase following distance to avoid hydroplaning.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Exercise.
note: Time is the only reliable way for the body to lower BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, signal, yield to vehicles already on the freeway, and merge when safe.

question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Is most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.,b:Depends on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream.,c:Is less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.
note: The effects of alcohol on reflexes and judgment depend on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not the type of beverage.

question: On slippery roads, what is the recommended action regarding speed?
options: a:Drive more quickly.,b:Drive the posted speed limit with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce your speed immediately when roads become slippery due to rain, snow, or ice; driving slower than the posted limit may be necessary.

question: If you are following a school bus or a large tank truck, what should you be prepared to do at railroad crossings?
options: a:Pass them on the right.,b:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.,c:Expect them to speed up.,d:Sound your horn to get them to move.
note: Passenger vans, buses, and larger trucks are required to stop at railroad crossings; maintain a safe distance and be prepared to stop as well.

question: True or False: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your crash risk.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE,c:Only if using hands-free,d:Depends on the driver's experience
note: Using a phone while driving is a distraction and significantly increases the risk of being involved in a crash.

question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb should your vehicle be?
options: a:No more than 10 inches.,b:No more than 12 inches.,c:No more than 18 inches.,d:No more than 24 inches.
note: Your vehicle should be within 12 inches of the curb when parallel parked so it is visible and safely positioned.

question: To ensure your physical condition won't impair driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep physically fit and have routine physical exams.,b:Know how any medication affects your driving, and drive within your limits.,c:Ignore minor health issues until after driving.,d:Both a and b.
note: Drivers should be aware of physical limitations, stay fit, have regular exams, understand medication effects, and drive within safe limits.

question: Which statement is true about adjusting driving for weather?
options: a:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
note: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving accordingly: reduce speed in rain or fog and be mindful of vehicles around you.

question: Is the most common mistake when backing up failing to look both ways behind you?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Mirrors do not give a full view when backing; turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,b:It impairs your thinking ability.,c:It slows your reaction time.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, slows reaction time, and can produce a false sense of confidence while degrading coordination and vision.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before roadways?
options: a:True — ramps and bridges can freeze quicker and need extra caution.,b:False
note: Bridges and ramps are exposed to air on both sides and can develop ice faster than roadways, so reduce speed and be cautious.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic at a railroad crossing with no signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:There is enough space to clear the tracks so you won't stop on them.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
note: Before entering tracks, make sure your vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping; never pass another vehicle near the crossing and always look for trains.

question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and may force your way in.,b:You should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:You must come to a full stop at the end of the ramp.,d:You may drive on the shoulder to merge.
note: Vehicles already on the interstate have the right-of-way; use the ramp to accelerate and merge safely into traffic when there is a gap.

question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as which traffic control?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A crossbuck is treated like a yield sign: you must yield the right-of-way to any approaching trains and railroad equipment.

question: When a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a multilane highway separated by a median, drivers:
options: a:Must stop and wait for the flashing lights to stop.,b:Must stop until the bus begins moving.,c:Must stop until the stop arm is lifted.,d:May continue driving without stopping.
note: If the highway is separated by a median or divider, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop; if not separated, traffic in both directions must stop for a stopped bus with red flashing lights.

question: What does an \End school zone\" sign indicate?"
options: a:The school zone reduced speed limit has ended.,b:The start of a 20 mph school speed zone.,c:Increased danger of encountering children ahead.,d:A required stop for school buses only.
note: An \End school zone\" sign marks the end of the reduced speed school zone; do not exceed the posted limit for that sign."

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,c:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
note: Only time reduces BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower BAC or make you sober.

question: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic control devices govern the flow of traffic and must be obeyed to ensure safety and order on the road.

question: How serious is drinking and driving as a traffic safety problem?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving after drinking is a serious safety hazard that greatly increases crash risk and legal consequences.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in back of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of the vehicle.
note: Keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle to allow time to react to hazards and avoid collisions.

question: At night when an oncoming vehicle approaches, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is approaching or when following closely; use low beams to avoid blinding others.

question: Are drivers required to yield to children playing in the street?
options: a:True — drive with extreme caution where children may be present.,b:False
note: Exercise great caution and reduce speed near children, schools, and playgrounds as they may unpredictably enter the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady red light.,c:A police officer directing traffic.,d:A stop sign.
note: A person authorized to direct traffic, such as a police officer, overrides traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings. Always follow their directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.,b:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your directional signal.
note: Before changing lanes, always check mirrors and glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot, and signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.,b:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.,c:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
note: Use the ramp to accelerate to the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway when merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When arriving at a four-way stop, must you yield to drivers who reached the intersection before you?
options: a:No — you may proceed if the lane is clear.,b:Yes — yield to drivers who arrived earlier.,c:Only if they signal you to go.,d:Only if they are to your right.
note: At a four-way stop, drivers must yield to vehicles that arrived before them and then proceed in turn.

question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You might not see the road between vehicles.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You might not see the vehicle's turn signals.,d:All of the above.
note: Following too closely reduces your ability to see and react; you may not have enough stopping distance if traffic halts suddenly.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:Because they can be difficult to see and are more vulnerable in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws than vehicles.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users are harder to spot and are more exposed; be extra attentive to avoid collisions.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:A good driving habit.,b:An unnecessary maneuver.,c:A bad driving habit.
note: Turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes is a proper and necessary safety habit; do not rely solely on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only at intersections.,c:Only on hills.
note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility is limited.

question: Is alcohol the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:True — alcohol is the leading cause.,b:False — it is not a major factor.,c:True but only at night.,d:False — speeding is the leading cause.
note: Alcohol is a leading contributing factor in fatal crashes because it impairs vision, reaction time, and judgment.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that may affect safety, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.,c:Correct the defect when you can afford it.
note: Any defect that jeopardizes safe operation should be repaired right away; do not delay needed maintenance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate into the first clear lane and then cross the others.,b:Wait until you can clearly see all lanes you must cross before turning.,c:Proceed when a driver gestures you to go.,d:Edge forward into the intersection until the view clears.
note: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can safely complete the turn.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: If another driver is trying to pass you, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the roadway to let them pass.,b:Signal when it is safe for them to pass and adjust speed so they can return to the lane.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake hard to block their pass.
note: When another vehicle is passing, keep steady and check for oncoming traffic; adjust speed to make it safe for the passing vehicle to return to your lane.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Railroad crossings.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing and requires you to yield to any approaching trains.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and then proceed if the way is clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,d:Turn only after signaling.
note: A red arrow means drivers must stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow unless posted otherwise.

question: Which of these does NOT typically happen after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Slowed reflexes and reaction time.,b:Distorted judgment of speed and distance.,c:Increased alertness.,d:Reduced ability to recover from glare.
note: Alcohol decreases alertness, impairs reflexes and judgment, and makes recovery from headlights slower.

question: If a vehicle with anti-lock brakes (ABS) begins to lose traction on a slippery road, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal and steer out of danger.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the accelerator.,d:Release the brake pedal immediately.
note: In ABS-equipped vehicles, press firmly on the brake pedal and hold it. The ABS will automatically modulate braking so you can steer while braking.

question: If involved in a serious crash, what actions are required?
options: a:Stop, call 911 if anyone is injured, and report to law enforcement if required.,b:Drive on if no one is injured.,c:Determine if anyone is injured before stopping.
note: Stop and move to safety if possible; call emergency services for injuries and report the crash to police if there is injury, death, or significant property damage.

question: Which feature is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road,b:Flashing yellow lights,c:Arrow markings showing lane use,d:Flashing red lights
note: Lane-use arrows, either painted on the pavement or on overhead signs, indicate which lanes are designated for turning or going straight.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates.
note: Not all crossings have active warning devices like lights and gates, and it is illegal to go around lowered gates or ignore flaggers and signs.

question: What does a flashing red light in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign.,b:The traffic signal is broken.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light requires the driver to stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe—just like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to be aware of your intention.,b:Signal just after you start changing lanes.,c:Signal only at intersections.,d:There is no need to signal when passing.
note: Signal early so other drivers know your intentions well in advance of changing lanes to pass.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,d:Left turns are prohibited.
note: A flashing yellow arrow means left turns are permitted but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: When backing up, what is the safest technique to ensure you can see behind the vehicle?
options: a:Open the driver's door and look back while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,d:Flash your lights while backing to warn pedestrians.
note: When backing, turn your head and look through the rear window so you can see obstacles or children. Do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors and check behind the vehicle before you get in.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.,b:Work harder to steer, reduce your speed, drive to a safe area, and stop.,c:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
note: If power steering stops, it will be harder to steer; slow down, carefully steer to a safe area, and stop to inspect the vehicle.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and the owner cannot be located, what must you do?
options: a:Must stay until the police arrive.,b:Have done as much as you can.,c:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and accident details.
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a written notice with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Keep a steady pace.
note: Avoid lingering in another vehicle's blind spot; either move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.

question: Is it legal to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving at night with only parking lights is unlawful; headlights must be used when visibility is reduced by darkness.

question: On a road with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian use?
options: a:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:Side of the road with the lightest traffic.,c:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and drivers can see them.

question: Is smoking or preparing to smoke while driving distracting?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Handling cigarettes, lighters, or other smoking materials takes your hands and eyes off driving tasks and is a distraction.

question: Under which conditions must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating,b:Directed to do so by a flagger,c:It is controlled by a stop sign,d:Any of the above (flagger, stop sign, or active signals/gates)
note: You must stop when directed by a flagger, when a stop sign controls the crossing, or when flashing red signals and gates are active.

question: Under normal driving conditions, what following distance should drivers maintain?
options: a:Four seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Five seconds.
note: Use the three-second rule under normal conditions to maintain a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,d:All of the above
note: Use turn signals whenever you make lateral movements or enter traffic so other road users know your intentions.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A single broken white line indicates lane changes and passing are allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: Should you use high beam headlights while driving in fog?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Do not use high beams in fog; they reflect off moisture and worsen visibility. Use low beams or fog lights instead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never.,b:When legally passing another vehicle on a multilane highway with a posted speed limit of 55 mph or higher.,c:When there is no police officer present.,d:When traffic is light.
note: Generally it is illegal to exceed posted limits; however Minnesota law allows an increase of up to 10 mph when lawfully passing on a multilane highway with a posted speed limit of 55 mph or higher.

question: What is the “No zone” in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus where the vehicle cannot see you.,b:A special speed zone around trucks.,c:A roadway with restrictions on stereo volume.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots on all sides called “No zones”; avoid lingering in these areas where the truck driver cannot see you.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:No passing in either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing allowed only at hilltops.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate traffic in both directions; you may not cross them to pass from either direction.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, do larger vehicles have larger blind spots?
options: a:Yes — larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,b:No — they have smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots.
note: Larger vehicles such as trucks and buses have bigger blind spots; be cautious when near them and avoid lingering beside them.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by which color lines?
options: a:Red,b:White,c:Yellow.
note: White lines (solid or broken) separate lanes that move in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze quickly in cold/wet conditions?
options: a:Flat areas.,b:Shaded areas under trees or buildings.,c:Curvy sections.
note: Sections of road shaded by trees or buildings freeze faster and stay icy longer than sun-exposed areas; use extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which is the correct practice?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal (at least 100 feet in residential areas), check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before turning left at an intersection?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: Before turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and only turn when the way is clear.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what is the correct behavior?
options: a:Keep moving and maintain focus on your driving.,b:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep your attention on driving and move safely past the scene.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Only drivers who are already in the intersection.,c:No one — left turns always have right-of-way.
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians or others occupying the intersection before you proceed.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to tell the driver you are there.,b:Yield to the transit vehicle so it can safely re-enter traffic.,c:Speed up to block it from merging.,d:Ignore the signal and maintain your lane.
note: You must yield to a transit vehicle signaling to re-enter traffic after loading or unloading passengers by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping as needed.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high-beam headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Directly into the headlights.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road and the edge of your lane.,d:Toward the left side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while still maintaining enough view to stay on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions are prohibited while stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stopping to drop off passengers or to check an address.,b:Stopping briefly to let someone out when traffic is light.,c:Backing up to reach an entrance ramp.,d:All of the above are prohibited.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason. If you miss an exit or turn, do not back up or make a U-turn; continue to the next safe location.

question: What is the correct procedure when changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,b:Always use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.,d:Change lanes without signaling to be faster.
note: On interstates, signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes; only stop on the shoulder for emergencies.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Continue normally through the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with care.,c:Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution: slow down, look, and proceed through the intersection with care.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:False — night riding is more hazardous.,b:True
note: Bicycles are harder to see at night even with lights and reflectors; both cyclists and drivers must be especially alert after dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection on a green light but oncoming traffic is heavy, what should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection instead.,b:Wait at the marked crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Enter the intersection and wait there for a safe gap before turning,d:Begin the turn and stop halfway
note: If the light is green and no vehicle ahead plans to turn left, you may enter the intersection to wait for a gap in oncoming traffic; do not block the crosswalk.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights, and fog lights if equipped.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams and fog lights in fog; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: If you drink socially, what measure helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Arrange a sober ride home, designate a driver, or use alternative transportation; coffee or showers do not sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a reduced conflict intersection, are left turns allowed?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if signed,d:Only during daylight
note: Reduced conflict intersections are designed so drivers make right turns followed by a U-turn to change direction; left turns are not made directly at the intersection.

question: How should drivers respond to a steady green arrow traffic signal?
options: a:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,b:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,c:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow means you may make the indicated turn; yield to any pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before completing the turn.

question: Do pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way?
options: a:True — they always have right-of-way.,b:False — not always, but pedestrians have right-of-way at intersections and crosswalks.,c:Only if the crosswalk is marked.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at intersections or crosswalks whether marked or unmarked; drivers must yield.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow down, look, listen, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,d:Ignore the tracks unless there are lights.
note: Approach railroad crossings with care: look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore signals.

question: When faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what is the safest action?
options: a:Let the car pass and then pass the bike.,b:Pull onto the shoulder.,c:Split the difference between the hazards.
note: Avoid dealing with two hazards at once: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass, then safely pass the bicyclist when there is adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:Only when turning left into a driveway.,b:When it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.,c:Never under any circumstance.,d:Only to pass a disabled vehicle.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

question: If another driver is tailgating you, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Move to the right if there is an open lane.,b:If no right lane exists, wait until clear and then reduce speed slowly to encourage them to pass.,c:Never slow down abruptly.,d:All of the above.
note: If tailgated, move over if possible; if not, slow down gradually when safe to encourage the tailgater to pass and avoid sudden braking.

question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spot, you should:
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; do not rely only on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?
options: a:When the entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.,b:Immediately after passing, regardless of visibility.,c:Only at the next traffic signal.
note: Do not move back in front of a passed vehicle until you can see the whole vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is true?
options: a:As speed increases, tires become less effective and hydroplaning risk rises.,b:Water has no effect if you have high-quality tires.,c:Deep water is less hazardous than shallow water.,d:Driving faster improves traction.
note: Higher speeds reduce tire effectiveness at displacing water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning on wet surfaces.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow and proceed with caution rather than stop?
options: a:Flashing yellow light.,b:Flashing red light.,c:Solid yellow light.,d:Solid red light.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; drivers should slow down and proceed with caution.

question: When traffic is merging near a construction zone using a zipper merge, what is the recommended driver behavior?
options: a:Stay in your lane until the point of merge, then take turns with other vehicles.,b:Merge into the adjacent lane as early as possible.,c:Change lanes immediately when you see a 'Lane closed ahead' sign.,d:Stop at the 'Lane closed ahead' sign and wait for traffic to clear.
note: When you see a 'Lane closed ahead' sign, remain in your lane until the merge point and then alternate with other drivers in a smooth zipper fashion.

question: Which color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: Yellow pavement markings separate opposing directions of traffic; white separates lanes moving the same direction.

question: A downward-facing triangular sign generally means:
options: a:Indicate school zones.,b:Tells drivers to yield.,c:Indicate construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign, meaning you must give the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,b:Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.,d:Activate your signal and immediately move into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, verify the lane is clear, then move over when it is safe.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what is the first step?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.,c:Turn your wheels to the right.
note: After finding a suitable space, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space, signal, then begin steering into the space.

question: Which statement best describes drivers who have consumed alcohol?
options: a:They are always aware of the risks.,b:They typically lack sufficient control over their bodies and judgment.,c:They become better drivers due to increased confidence.,d:They are more alert than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time; intoxicated drivers do not have sufficient control.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or historical interest?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Brown.,d:Green.
note: Brown signs are used to indicate recreational and cultural interest areas, such as parks and historic sites.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.,b:Follow the traffic light regardless of the officer.,c:Honk at the officer to confirm instructions.
note: An officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals; obey the officer's instructions for safety and legal compliance.

question: Which of these is recommended for safer night driving?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Avoid driving only if you are tired.,c:Ensure your headlights are functioning properly.,d:Use high beams at all times.
note: At night, reduced visibility makes working headlights essential; also increase following distance and avoid driving when fatigued.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Stop at the marked stop line.
note: A red light means stop: you must stop before entering the intersection, at any stop line, or before any crosswalk.

question: What lane width is a motorcycle entitled to use on the roadway?
options: a:Half the lane width.,b:A marked bicycle lane only.,c:The same full lane width as other vehicles.,d:Only the right edge of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width just like any other vehicle and should be given the same space.

question: When stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when may you proceed?
options: a:As soon as the first train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing.,c:Proceed if no gate is down.,d:Cross immediately if lights stop flashing.
note: At crossings with more than one track, wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding; another train may be approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Not cross the centerline.,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.,c:Use the shoulder.,d:Only pass when you can safely use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete the pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires moving into the oncoming traffic lane; only pass when you can do so safely and legally.

question: Are blue, flashing, or strobe lights permitted on personal vehicles?
options: a:False — only authorized maintenance or emergency vehicles may display them.,b:True
note: Special colored or flashing lights are reserved for authorized emergency and maintenance vehicles and are not permitted on private vehicles.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
note: At passive crossings (no lights/gates), slow, look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop; never shift gears while crossing if avoidable.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Following a motorcycle.,b:Exiting an expressway.,c:Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
note: Increase your following distance when a large vehicle blocks your view ahead, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when someone is tailgating you, or when bicycle/motorcycle riders are ahead.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road from either direction when its stop arm is extended and signals are active.

question: Is it permissible to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Yes, as long as you are not driving.,b:Yes, if you are in the backseat.,c:No — consuming alcohol or possessing an open container in areas occupied by driver or passengers is prohibited.,d:Yes, if you are in a pickup truck bed.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage in areas of the vehicle normally occupied by the driver or passengers on public roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:Solid green circular light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.,d:A steady red light.
note: A green left-turn arrow gives you the right-of-way to turn; oncoming traffic is required to stop for turning vehicles.

question: Orange-colored road signs usually indicate:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:School zone signs.
note: Orange signs warn drivers about highway work zones and related hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which steps should you take?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Only signal; mirrors are optional.,c:Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light.
note: Before changing lanes you should signal in advance, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

question: You should leave a larger space cushion than usual when stopping:
options: a:On an incline.,b:At an intersection.,c:At a stop sign.,d:When parking.
note: When stopped on an uphill slope, the vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic moves; leave extra space to prevent collisions.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
options: a:10 feet,b:20 feet,c:40 feet
note: Drivers may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection so that the vehicle is visible to traffic from both directions.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect driving?
options: a:It creates distractions that make vehicle control and lane keeping more difficult.,b:It makes drivers better because they are not hungry.,c:It results in no driving errors.
note: Eating and drinking divert your hands and eyes from driving tasks, increasing the chance of lane departures and crashes.

question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians who are walking against the traffic light?
options: a:True — motorists need not yield.,b:False — drivers must always yield to pedestrians.,c:Only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,d:Only during daytime hours.
note: You must yield to pedestrians; be mindful that pedestrians may cross against signals and you must take steps to avoid collisions.

question: How should drivers view railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross, as it is unlikely that a train will be coming.,b:Dangerous.,c:Safe locations to park a car.
note: Railroad crossings are potentially dangerous; always look and listen for approaching trains and obey all signals and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete your turn?
options: a:In the center of the street.,b:In the left lane of the one-way street.,c:In the right lane of the one-way street.,d:Into the bicycle lane.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from, usually the left lane of the one-way street.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should a driver do?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: When approaching a school crossing, be alert for children and be ready to stop; yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.,b:Do not immediately use your brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, avoid braking suddenly, slow gradually, and steer to a safe place to stop and inspect the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and are not in the proper lane to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes; continue to the next intersection and make turns from the appropriate lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane heading toward you, you should:
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and accelerate.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.,d:Flash your lights and maintain speed
note: Honk to attract attention, try to escape to the right, and brake firmly; swerving left can increase the risk of a head-on collision.

question: What should you do when rain starts while you are driving?
options: a:Slow down and turn on headlights; if visibility is very poor, pull off and wait.,b:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through quickly.
note: Reduce speed, use headlights for visibility, and if rain severely limits sight, safely pull over and stop until it eases.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the immediate correct response?
options: a:Reach down to free the pedal with your hand.,b:Shift into park and then call for help.,c:Shift to neutral, apply steady braking, and pull off the road when safe.,d:Turn off the ignition while still moving.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral, hold steady pressure on the brakes, steer safely off the road, and then turn off the engine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following actions should you take when preparing to make a left turn?
options: a:Signal, check for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and yield as needed.,b:Signal and immediately increase speed.,c:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,d:Signal and move into the right lane before turning.
note: When making a left turn, signal several seconds in advance, watch for oncoming traffic and pedestrians, move into the proper lane, and yield until your path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:You must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:You may drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,c:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,d:You may only turn right on green.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn, but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic as required.

question: If you stop on the roadside at night, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights and emergency flashers.,b:Turn off all your lights.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: If you stop along the road at night, keep your low beams on and use your emergency flashers so other road users can see you.

question: If the driver ahead appears distracted (one hand on the wheel, talking to a passenger), you should:
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Know they are reducing their safety margin.,c:Avoid following them or copying their behavior.,d:All of the above
note: Distracted drivers increase crash risk—allow extra space, be aware they have a reduced safety margin, and do not imitate their behavior.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Exercise extreme caution and pass slowly to avoid startling it.,b:No special action is required.,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible.
note: When encountering animals on the road, slow down and pass with care to avoid startling them and causing unpredictable movements.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians under what circumstances?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,c:Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly; pedestrians have the right-of-way in many situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:On a narrow bridge.,b:If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,c:Even if it means driving off the pavement.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is room to pass safely, or on multilane roads with two or more lanes traveling in the same direction.

question: Why should car drivers be especially cautious around large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They never need extra room to maneuver.,d:They are always easier to pass than cars.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and, because of their size and weight, require more distance to maneuver and stop. Avoid lingering beside or close behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Lane-use control signals showing a green arrow tell drivers:
options: a:Drivers should not drive in this lane.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:Drivers may use this lane because it is open.
note: A green arrow over a lane means that lane is open to traffic in the direction of the arrow; drivers may use it normally.

question: Is it legal to pass a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When a school bus is using flashing red lights you must stop before reaching the bus and remain stopped until the lights are turned off; on divided highways with a median, opposite-side traffic may not have to stop.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to get out of their way.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to prevent them passing you.,d:Brake-check them to slow them down.
note: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's path—move over when safe and avoid making eye contact or gestures that could escalate the situation.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:Traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs with black symbols warn of road conditions or hazards ahead needing caution.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement signify for drivers in that lane?
options: a:Drivers may choose to make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must always stop before following the arrow.,d:Arrows apply only when traffic lights are out of service.
note: An arrow painted within a travel lane indicates that drivers in that lane must make the movement shown, subject to traffic signals and signs.

question: Which is true about emergency vehicles?
options: a:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.,b:May follow each other.,c:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles with lights/sirens, follow loudspeaker instructions, and be aware emergency vehicles often operate in groups.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:As close as possible to the right side of the road.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.
note: When preparing to turn right, get as close to the right curb or edge of the roadway as safely possible.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Go the same speed.,c:Slow down to allow room in front so the driver can pass easily.
note: When someone wants to pass, slow slightly to give the passing driver room to complete the maneuver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.,b:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,c:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.
note: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway before entering from a driveway or private road; do not force your way into traffic.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto a shoulder, how should you return to the roadway?
options: a:Brake hard and sharply steer back onto the pavement.,b:Stop on the shoulder and re-enter when safe.,c:Slow down without braking sharply and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,d:Accelerate and swerve back onto the road.
note: Reduce speed without heavy braking, check traffic, and carefully steer back onto the pavement to avoid losing control.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left or right side mirror only.,b:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move to check the blind spot.,c:Check only the rearview mirror.,d:Honk to alert other drivers instead of checking.
note: To check blind spots, glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move so you can see areas not visible in mirrors.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a black symbol indicate?
options: a:That drivers must stop.,b:That the indicated action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers must yield.,d:That parking is allowed at certain times.
note: A red circle with a slash across a symbol indicates the action shown is prohibited by law.

question: 'Highway hypnosis' can result from what driving behavior?
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: Staring at the same point on a highway for long periods can lead to 'highway hypnosis', reducing alertness; keep your eyes moving.

question: How often should you stop to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Every two hours for a short break.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Drive with one eye open at a time.
note: To avoid fatigue, stop about every two hours to rest, stretch, and refresh; if drowsy, find a safe place to stop.

question: What is the first control you should adjust, if needed, when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror.,b:Your seat so you can see the road clearly.,c:The steering wheel.,d:Your radio.
note: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable, can reach the controls, and have a clear view of the road; then adjust mirrors and steering wheel as needed.

question: As alcohol builds up in your system, what happens?
options: a:Makes you feel less confident.,b:Slows down your reactions.,c:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
note: Alcohol slows reaction times, impairs judgment, and increases your likelihood of making driving errors.

question: Which best defines defensive driving?
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.,b:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c:Defending yourself against poor drivers by rushing ahead in traffic.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking steps to avoid collisions and conflicts with other road users.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: The statement 'The best way to avoid loss of control under wet conditions is to increase your vehicle's speed' is:
options: a:False,b:True
note: Hydroplaning risk increases with speed; you should reduce speed in wet conditions to avoid loss of control.

question: If a railroad crossing lacks active warning devices, you should slow down, look, and listen.
options: a:False,b:True
note: If a crossing has no electric flashing lights or gates, slow down, look in both directions, and listen for trains before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone,b:Only when driving in rural areas,c:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
note: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic; you may be cited for driving too slowly.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks even for a short time when moving with a line of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never stop on railroad tracks; always ensure there is space on the far side before crossing to avoid being trapped on the tracks.

question: What color is most commonly used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols to alert drivers of upcoming conditions.

question: Which location is unlawful for parking?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:On a hill.
note: It is illegal to park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes; follow local parking restrictions and stay within 12 inches of the curb when parking on the street.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is accurate?
options: a:You should never place a rear-facing infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.,b:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.,c:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,d:All of the above
note: Always fasten seat belts and use appropriate child restraints; children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in a rear seat and never place a rear-facing infant where a front airbag could deploy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering and driving in a roundabout, what should you do?
options: a:Stop inside the roundabout.,b:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.,c:Drive clockwise around the central island.
note: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise; enter from the right, yield to traffic already in the roundabout, and proceed around the island until your exit.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,b:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.,c:Avoid sudden stops.
note: Avoid sudden stops by gradually releasing the accelerator and braking smoothly; check mirrors to be aware of traffic behind you.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you do when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Always insist that vehicles stop for you in a crosswalk.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.,d:Assume vehicles will always stop for you.
note: Although pedestrians have right-of-way in marked crosswalks, do not enter the roadway in front of approaching vehicles; wait until it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does 'yield' sometimes mean you must stop if you cannot merge safely into traffic?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When required to yield, you must stop if necessary to merge safely into the flow of traffic without causing a hazard.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, reduce speed, and pull to a safe stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator to slow, avoid heavy braking until you are slow, and steer safely off the road.

question: How does being distracted affect a driver's reaction to hazards?
options: a:It usually causes slower reactions to hazards.,b:It never causes danger.,c:It causes drivers to drive faster.
note: Any distraction will slow your reactions and impair driving ability, increasing the likelihood of crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.,b:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers should slow down below the posted limit when conditions are not ideal.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally.
note: When encountering a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow, yield, and be prepared to stop to protect them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what is the appropriate response?
